albums.title: Senior
albums.reason: With over 1,000 all-time plays Röyksopp are one of your deepest loves — Senior is their most introspective and ambient record, a side of them that rewards a proper deep-vault immersion.

albums.title: Orbital (The Blue Album)
albums.reason: Orbital sit at 777 all-time plays and you've already revisited the Brown Album — time to go back to where it all started with this landmark debut.

albums.title: First Impressions of Earth
albums.reason: The Strokes clock 652 all-time plays and you've already revisited Is This It and Room on Fire — this underrated third album is the natural next stop in the vault.

albums.title: Protection
albums.reason: Massive Attack have 534 all-time plays and you've already hit Mezzanine and Blue Lines — Protection is the warmer, more soulful side of their catalogue that deserves another spin.

albums.title: Dig Your Own Hole
albums.reason: The Chemical Brothers appear in your all-time top 50 at 556 plays — Dig Your Own Hole is their defining peak and a pure time-machine hit for this tier.

albums.title: Everything Is Wrong
albums.reason: Moby sits at 551 all-time plays and you've revisited Play and 18 already — Everything Is Wrong is the rawer, hungrier record from his catalogue that rewards a deep-vault dig.

albums.title: Moderat
albums.reason: Moderat are a clear all-time favourite across multiple records in your history — their self-titled debut is where the Apparat and Modeselektor worlds first collided and it's ripe for a recent-vault revisit.

albums.title: The North Borders
albums.reason: Bonobo has 440 all-time plays and 23 in the last year — The North Borders is his most lush and orchestral statement and fits the recent-vault window perfectly as a record worth returning to whole.

albums.title: Singularity
albums.reason: Jon Hopkins is confirmed in your world and Open Eye Signal is already recommended — Singularity is the album that surrounds it and one of the defining electronic records of the recent-vault era.

albums.title: Promises
albums.reason: Floating Points show up in your recent listening history and Elaenia was already recommended — Promises, his collaboration with Pharoah Sanders, is one of the most beloved records of the early 2020s and belongs in your recent vault.

albums.title: Persona
albums.reason: Rival Consoles feature in your previously recommended picks confirming you know the artist — Persona is his breakthrough full-length, richly melodic and emotionally direct, and fits the recent-vault timeframe perfectly.

albums.title: Portraits
albums.reason: Maribou State clock 434 all-time plays and sit in your all-time top 50 — Portraits is their earlier, more intimate record and a different angle on their sound that rewards a recent-vault return.

albums.title: Pole 3
albums.reason: Your deep love for Leftfield, Massive Attack and Underworld points straight at Stefan Betke's Pole project — Pole 3 is a masterclass in dubbed-out, glitchy bass music that sits in exactly the same atmospheric space.

albums.title: The Light 3000
albums.reason: Your all-time love for Plaid, Modeselektor and Orbital suggests a deep affinity for Berlin-school electronic craft — Schneider TM's The Light 3000 lives in that same melodic-machine world and is criminally overlooked.

albums.title: Substrata
albums.reason: Your reverence for Aphex Twin, Moby and Pink Floyd's atmospheric side points directly at Geir Jenssen's Biosphere — Substrata is one of the greatest ambient albums ever made and a perfect discovery for your vault.

albums.title: Cinemascope
albums.reason: Your all-time passion for Daft Punk, Leftfield and Orbital signals a love of machine-precise electronic architecture — Robert Henke's Monolake project and this album in particular is a landmark of Berlin minimal techno you'd likely adore.

albums.title: Electro-Soma
albums.reason: Your all-time love for Orbital, Aphex Twin and Leftfield traces directly back to the Warp Records early-90s constellation — B12's Electro-Soma is one of its most beautiful and overlooked entries.

albums.title: Power Clown
albums.reason: Fila Brazillia appeared in your previously recommended section meaning you've been circling this world — Power Clown is their warmest, most sun-drunk album and adjacent to your Basement Jaxx and Moby all-time loves.

albums.title: Ill Considered 8
albums.reason: Your recent arc through Portico Quartet, Yussef Dayes and Nubya Garcia points at the London jazz underground — Ill Considered's live-improv intensity is the rawer, more frenetic side of that scene and this album captures them at their best.

albums.title: Voice Notes
albums.reason: Your recent listening to Bill Withers, Charles Bradley and Erykah Badu confirms a deep pull toward soulful, intimate vocal music — Yazmin Lacey's Voice Notes EP is an essential piece of the UK neo-soul puzzle you'd love.

albums.title: Things Have Not Always Been This Way
albums.reason: Your recent immersion in Nils Frahm, Ben Lukas Boysen and Ólafur Arnalds points at a love of slow, spacious, melodic ambient — Spanish composer Suso Saiz made some of the deepest music in this vein decades before it was fashionable.

albums.title: It's a World Before You
albums.reason: Your recent pull toward Khruangbin, Makaya McCraven and St Germain suggests a love of jazz that swings and grooves — Kaidi Tatham is one of the most inventive figures in UK broken-beat jazz and this album is a brilliant entry point.

albums.title: Black Noise
albums.reason: Your recent listening to Dominik Eulberg, Max Cooper and Apparat signals a love of precise, atmospheric electronic music — Pantha du Prince's Black Noise is one of the most beautiful records in that world and a must-hear.

albums.title: Palme
albums.reason: Your recent listening to Ólafur Arnalds, Hania Rani and A Winged Victory for the Sullen shows a love of Nordic chamber and folk textures — his cousin Ólöf Arnalds makes quietly extraordinary music in an adjacent space that you'd likely adore.

albums.title: Come With Fierce Grace
albums.reason: Alabaster DePlume is your number one artist this month and this week by a wide margin — Come With Fierce Grace is the album you're clearly living inside right now and deserves a full dedicated listen.

albums.title: A La Sala
albums.reason: Khruangbin are your second most-played artist this month and A La Sala is your most-played album of the last 12 months — it's clearly a current cornerstone and belongs right here.

albums.title: Tower of Silence
albums.reason: Roberto Musci appeared in your most recent tracks this very week — Tower of Silence is a one-of-a-kind record that fits the slow, exploratory, cinematic mood you're clearly in right now.

albums.title: Living Fields
albums.reason: Portico Quartet are active in your current listening and Living Fields is their most atmospheric and patient record — it fits the slow, introspective space you're inhabiting this week perfectly.

albums.title: A Plane Over Woods
albums.reason: The Vernon Spring are your second most-played artist this week — A Plane Over Woods is the album you've been returning to and it captures the gentle, pastoral mood running through everything you're playing right now.

albums.title: Miniatures de Auto-Matic
albums.reason: Domenique Dumont showed up strongly in your last 7 days — this debut album is a perfect fit for the soft, unhurried, sun-bleached atmosphere you're clearly seeking right now.

songs.title: Only This Moment
songs.reason: With 1,062 all-time plays Röyksopp are one of your deepest constants — Only This Moment from The Understanding is one of their most soaring, emotionally overwhelming tracks.

songs.title: Risingson
songs.reason: Massive Attack clock 534 all-time plays and Mezzanine has already been recommended — Risingson is one of its most underplayed gems, coiled and hypnotic, and perfect for a deep vault revisit.

songs.title: Where Do I Begin
songs.reason: The Chemical Brothers are in your all-time top 50 and you've heard Surrender tracks already — Where Do I Begin from Dig Your Own Hole is their most achingly beautiful moment.

songs.title: Dark and Long
songs.reason: Underworld sit at 633 all-time plays and this early slow-burn anthem from dubnobasswithmyheadman is one of the most hypnotic things they ever made — a pure deep-vault drift.

songs.title: Lichen
songs.reason: Aphex Twin has 522 all-time plays and you know Xtal already — Lichen, from the same Selected Ambient Works Volume II record, is equally gorgeous and deserves its own moment.

songs.title: Rushing
songs.reason: Moby is deep in your all-time list at 551 plays — Rushing from Everything Is Wrong is one of the most euphoric moments in his catalogue and a perfect deep-vault pick.

songs.title: Emerald Rush
songs.reason: Jon Hopkins is confirmed in your world through your previously recommended history and Open Eye Signal is already in there — Emerald Rush from Singularity is its equal and deserves a slot in the recent vault.

songs.title: Silhouettes (I, II & III)
songs.reason: Floating Points show up in your recent listening and previously recommended history — Silhouettes from Elaenia is a slow-building, deeply emotional centrepiece track that fits the recent-vault era perfectly.

songs.title: Ghostmother
songs.reason: Moderat are a recurring all-time favourite and you've already picked up several of their tracks — Ghostmother from III is one of their most haunting and underplayed, perfect for the recent vault.

songs.title: Tongue
songs.reason: Maribou State clock 434 all-time plays and Tongue is one of their most beloved early tracks — hypnotic and warm, it sits perfectly in the recent-vault era and hasn't been duplicated in your previous recommendations.

songs.title: Baby
songs.reason: Four Tet have 27 plays in your last 12 months and you've already explored several of his records — Baby from New Energy is a fan favourite that hasn't appeared in your previously recommended list yet.

songs.title: Untravel
songs.reason: Rival Consoles appear in your previously recommended world and Untravel from Overflow is one of his most driving, emotionally charged pieces — it fits the recent vault era and the intensity you clearly respond to.

songs.title: Silberfisch
songs.reason: Your all-time love for Leftfield, Massive Attack and bass-heavy electronic music points directly at Pole's early micro-click dub work — Silberfisch is one of his most hypnotic and completely overlooked gems.

songs.title: Kobresia
songs.reason: Adjacent to your Aphex Twin and Pink Floyd ambient obsessions, Biosphere's Kobresia from Substrata is one of the most quietly devastating ambient tracks ever recorded — a genuine revelation.

songs.title: Cyan
songs.reason: Your all-time passion for the Warp and abstract electronic world via Orbital and Plaid maps perfectly onto Monolake's meticulous minimal techno — Cyan is a landmark track from Cinemascope.

songs.title: Musicology
songs.reason: Your all-time reverence for Orbital and Aphex Twin puts you exactly in the Warp Records early-90s universe where B12 lived — Musicology from Electro-Soma is one of the most soulful pieces of music from that era.

songs.title: The Light 3000
songs.reason: Your all-time love for Plaid and Modeselektor's more melodic electronic work points straight at Schneider TM — the title track is a gorgeous, unhurried piece of German electronica that would fit perfectly in your world.

songs.title: Mermaids
songs.reason: Fila Brazillia appeared in your previously recommended section confirming you know the artist — Mermaids from their catalogue is one of their most gorgeous individual moments and a different angle on the same trip.

songs.title: Don't Rush the Process
songs.reason: Your recent year of Khruangbin, Portico Quartet and St Germain suggests an appetite for jazz that breathes and moves — Kaidi Tatham's Don't Rush the Process is a blissful, soulful track from that same universe.

songs.title: Welt Am Draht
songs.reason: Your recent engagement with Dominik Eulberg and Max Cooper's precise electronic worlds aligns perfectly with Pantha du Prince — Welt Am Draht from Black Noise is one of its most beautiful, chiming moments.

songs.title: La Hora del Lobo
songs.reason: Your recent immersion in Nils Frahm, Joep Beving and Ben Lukas Boysen points at a hunger for deep, meditative ambient — Suso Saiz's La Hora del Lobo is from the same rarefied space and barely anyone knows it.

songs.title: Yoyogi Park
songs.reason: Your recent Tosca and DJ Koze listening confirms you love the warmer, deeper side of Kompakt's catalogue — the title track from Lawrence's album is a meditative, slow-building house gem you'd love.

songs.title: Emergence
songs.reason: Your recent arc through Portico Quartet and Yussef Dayes points at the explosive, improvisational side of UK jazz — Ill Considered's Emergence captures their live energy at its most visceral.

songs.title: If Only
songs.reason: Your recent deep listening to Bill Withers and Charles Bradley confirms a love of honest, emotionally direct soul — Yazmin Lacey's If Only is one of the most affecting UK neo-soul tracks in years.

songs.title: Levels Of Human
songs.reason: This track appeared in your most recent plays this very week — it's clearly living with you right now and belongs in the current mood as your most immediate signal.

songs.title: May Ninth
songs.reason: May Ninth is your single most-played track in the last 12 months — it's the perfect current-mood pick given how much you've been living with A La Sala this month.

songs.title: Burrow
songs.reason: Flaer are one of your most-played artists this week and Burrow appeared in your most recent tracks — it fits perfectly in the quiet, inward mood you're carrying right now.

songs.title: Nothing Can Stop Us
songs.reason: Nothing Can Stop Us was literally the last track you played — The Vernon Spring are a clear current obsession and this track is the centrepiece of that mood.

songs.title: Rack Railway To
songs.reason: Rack Railway To appeared in your most recent play history this week — Tower of Silence is clearly a current companion and this track captures its mysterious, cinematic atmosphere at its best.

songs.title: Comme Ça
songs.reason: Domenique Dumont showed up strongly in your last seven days and Comme Ça is one of their most unhurried, sun-dappled tracks — it fits the soft, drifting current mood running through everything you're playing.
